leaves.name: buzzardThm21Cor23V15
leaves.doc: y3-printed, consequence of Buzzard, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) Thm 2.1 and Cor. 2.3 at U = V1(5), where M_U d = 30 (author's preprint: Thm 2.1 p. 5, Cor. 2.3 p. 7): a proper smooth curve X over Z[1/30] with a closed immersion into some P^N over Z[1/30], and an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) over X with a V1(5)-structure (a section Q with 5Q = 0 and iota(3 + 2k)Q = 0, nonzero at every geometric point), universal for such data over every Z[1/30]-scheme S: exactly one g : S -> X over Z[1/30] admits an O-compatible cartesian square carrying Q' to Q, and that square is unique. Unprinted steps: Buzzard's V1(5) for a choice of his fixed kappa with kappa(3 + 2k) = diag(1, 0) mod 5 (README B-5); uniqueness of the square is the absence of automorphisms in the proof of Cor. 2.3 (Lemma 2.2); projective over the affine base gives the closed immersion; no polarization in the data. One of the eight rows that replace y3FullThreeRepZ30 (Y3Buzzard.y3FullThreeRepZ30_of_printed_min5); prints quoted and unprinted steps written out in ZInQKernel/Contrib/OneProof/Y3FullThreeRepZ30/README.md.

leaves.doc: y3-printed, Milne, Abelian varieties, in Cornell-Silverman (eds.), Arithmetic Geometry (Springer 1986), Prop. 20.7 at g = 2, n = 3 (p. 44 of the author's retyped edition): for an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) over a Z[1/30]-scheme S, iota(3), which is multiplication by 3 (proved: iotaHom_natCast), is finite and etale. leaves.name: buzzardFrameRepTorsor5
leaves.doc: y3-printed, consequence of Buzzard, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) section 1, the sentence after Def. 1.1 (M prime to d = 6, printed without proof): for an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) over a Z[1/30]-scheme S there are a closed subscheme Z of A, finite, etale and surjective over S, whose T-points are exactly the generators of full level-5 structures (P with 5P = 0 such that a |-> iota(a)P is a bijection O/5O -> A_t[5] at every geometric point t), and an action rho of G = (O/5O)^x on Z by iota of fixed lifts, with Z x G -> Z x_S Z an isomorphism (the torsor condition, as a kernel-pair square). Unprinted step: a full level structure alpha is determined by P = alpha(1), and is an isomorphism exactly when P generates on geometric fibres (README B-4). One of the eight rows that replace y3FullThreeRepZ30 (Y3Buzzard.y3FullThreeRepZ30_of_printed_min5); prints quoted and unprinted steps written out in ZInQKernel/Contrib/OneProof/Y3FullThreeRepZ30/README.md.

leaves.name: serreRigidityLevel3
leaves.doc: y3-printed, consequence of Milne, Abelian varieties (1986) Cor. 2.2 (p. 3) and Prop. 17.5(b) (p. 37 of the author's retyped edition) with Buzzard 1997 section 1 (the canonical principal polarization, preprint p. 3): let theta be an automorphism over S of an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) commuting with iota(O), s : Spec k -> S a geometric point with char k not 2 or 3, and P in A_s(k) such that a |-> iota(a)P is a bijection O/3O -> A_s[3]; if theta fixes P, it fixes every point of A_s(k). Unprinted steps: theta fixes 0 since iota(0) = 0, so it is a homomorphism on the fibre; theta preserves Buzzard's polarization by its uniqueness (README B-2, B-3). One of the eight rows that replace y3FullThreeRepZ30 (Y3Buzzard.y3FullThreeRepZ30_of_printed_min5); prints quoted and unprinted steps written out in ZInQKernel/Contrib/OneProof/Y3FullThreeRepZ30/README.md.

leaves.doc: y3-printed, Milne, Abelian varieties (1986) Cor. 20.2(a) (p. 43 of the author's retyped edition), restricted to locally noetherian bases: a morphism over S of FECs (abelian schemes of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism from O) carrying the unit section to the unit section is a homomorphism. The printed proof applies Prop. 20.1, stated for a connected base; Lan, Harvard thesis (2008) Cor. 1.3.1.6 states it over any base, citing GIT Cor. 6.4.
